plain: An unfair leaning for or against a person or idea

webster.text: A weight on the side of a bowl which turns it from a straight line.

more.text: A leaning of the mind; inclination; prepossession; propensity towards an object, not leaving the mind indifferent; as, education gives a bias to the mind.
That which causes the mind to lean or incline from a state of indifference, to a particular object or course.

example.quote: If any further arguments were necessary to evince the improbability of such a bias, it might be found in the nature of the agency of the Senate in the business of appointments.
